title: Your Right to Information
tagline: How to ask public offices for information you need.
description: Public offices hold information that belongs to the people. Learn what you can ask for, how to write a simple request, and what steps to take if your request is refused.
outcomes: Understand what information you can ask for
Keep a copy and a record of your request
Know what to do if you are refused
Follow the right steps to appeal

lessons.title: Information you can ask for
lessons.body:
Public offices keep information that belongs to the people. In many cases you have a right to ask for it.

## What this means
You can ask a public office for information such as how a service works, what a project will cost, or the steps in a process. You do not always need to give a reason.

## What to expect
The office should help you or explain how to make a request. Some information is protected, for example personal details of other people, but much of it can be shared.
key_points: Public information belongs to the people
You can ask how a service or project works
You often do not need to give a reason
lessons.try_it: Think of one thing about a public service you would like to understand better.

lessons.title: Writing a simple request
lessons.body:
A clear request is easier to answer. You do not need big words.

## What to include
Say who you are, what information you want, and how you would like to receive it. Be specific: name the project, office or time period. Keep it short.

## Keep a copy
Write or type your request and keep a copy. If you hand it in, ask for a stamp or a note that it was received. If you send it, keep the message.
key_points: Say who you are and what you want
Be specific about the project or office
Keep a copy of your request
Ask for proof that it was received
lessons.try_it: Draft two sentences asking for one piece of public information you care about.

lessons.title: If they say no
lessons.body:
Sometimes a request is refused or ignored. There are calm steps you can take.

## Ask for the reason
If you are refused, ask for the reason in writing. A reason helps you know what to do next.

## Follow the next step
Ask the office how to appeal or who to take it to next. Keep your copy and the reason. If you are still stuck, a civil society organisation or a legal aid service may be able to guide you.
key_points: Ask for the reason for a refusal in writing
Ask how to appeal or who to go to next
Keep your copies and the reason
Seek help from a civil society or legal aid service
lessons.try_it: Write down one place or person you could ask for help if a request is refused.

quiz.question: When you ask a public office for information, you usually:
options: Do not always need to give a reason
quiz.explanation: You often do not need to give a reason. Much public information can be shared on request.

quiz.question: If your request for information is refused, a good step is to:
options: Ask for the reason and how to appeal
quiz.explanation: Ask for the reason in writing and how to appeal or who to take it to next.
